description:
FILED s484 (Fable review of s473t5a, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main 186134ce (before #1650) and on the s473t5a tree 17d831fe (after it).  #1650 made the WHOLE container `@119797` a declared ordinary global; the ELEMENT spelling was not in its scope.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    no strict; @119797 = (1,2,3);
    print "a:", $119797[1], " b:$119797[1] c:", scalar(@119797), "\n";
    perl:  a:2 b:2 c:3
    PCL :  a: b: c:3          <- both the CODE path and the INTERPOLATION path

EMISSION (read, not guessed):  (p-aref (p-high-capture 119797) 1)
So `$119797[1]` is lowered as the capture-group scalar `$119797` followed by an array subscript.  perl's rule: `$NAME[...]` / `$NAME{...}` is an element of @NAME / %NAME for EVERY legal name, and an all-digit name is legal for `@`/`%` (#1650's probed rule: `0` or `[1-9][0-9]*`); only the BARE `$NNN` is the capture group.  The same rule already holds for `$1[0]`?  -- probe it: perl reads `$1[0]` as element 0 of @1 too (perldata: "$1[0]" is @1's element), so the fix is the ordinary "sigil + subscript = element of the container" reading applied to the digit name class, in BOTH consumers (the PExpr term reader and Pl::InterpScan -- #237's one scanner), never a per-consumer special case.

Discriminate first: which of the two consumers takes the capture arm -- the term parser (`$119797[1]` in code) or the interp scanner (`"$119797[1]"`) -- and whether `$1[0]` / `$1{k}` take the same arm (they are the common spelling in real code: `$1[0]` is rare but `"$1[0]"` in a string appears in sprintf-heavy code).  ONE fix at the digit-name class (#1650 put it in `$VAR_TOKEN_RX`; the term reader and the scanner need the same "followed by [ or { => container element" rule).
BAR: the probe above + `$1[0]`/`"$1[0]"` after a successful match with @1 populated + `%12` twin (blocked on #1680, PPI) + a real capture `"$1"` unchanged, vs perl; guard rows beside #1650's in `Pl/t/global-partition-01.t`; corpus-diff + emission-ab (an emission change) + the full sweep.  SIZE: S.
subject: `$119797[1]` / `$12{k}` (an ELEMENT of the all-digit container @119797 / %12) is emitted as a subscript of the CAPTURE GROUP `$119797` -- the `$`-spelling half of #1650
